The post Miki Kawamura: a 19-year-old’s peace network brings ice cream to a Nobel summit first appeared on The Optimist Daily: Making Solutions the News.
articles.content:
BY THE OPTIMIST DAILY EDITORIAL TEAM

This article is part of The Optimist Daily’s Local Changemakers 2026 series, spotlighting changemakers 30 and under.

What does peace taste like? At the 20th World Summit of Nobel Peace Laureates, held in Rome from December 1 to 4, Miki Kawamura plans to let visitors decide for themselves. PeaceCream, a pop-up she has developed through her Youth Peace Ambassadors program in collaboration with Japan’s Goi Peace Foundation, gives each ice cream flavor a value tied to peace, such as love, hope, gratitude, or compassion. Participants think about what peace means to them, then build their own cup from the flavors and toppings that represent the values they want to bring into the world. “What if we could make peace something people can taste, feel, and share?” Miki asked when she described the idea to The Optimist Daily.

The concept is playful, but the conviction behind it runs through everything Miki has built since she was 18. In her view, peace has been left too long to political debates and international institutions. “It should become a part of our everyday lives, something we can experience, practice, and create together,” she said.

Youth Peace Ambassadors begins with the individual

A boarding school with students from 80 countries

Miki graduated in 2025 from UWC ISAK Japan, an international boarding school in rural Japan whose students come from more than 80 countries. Living alongside classmates from so many backgrounds taught her that peace grows less from agreement than from a common aim, a lesson she later laid out in a DailyGood essay titled “I’m 18. Here’s What I’ve Learned About Peace.” As she put it there, “Our differences may sometimes divide us, but a shared desire for peace has the power to bring us back.”

From one gap year to more than 100 countries

She founded Youth Peace Ambassadors in June 2025, during a gap year that also included an internship at the Goi Peace Foundation, one of Japan’s longest-running peace organizations. The premise is that peace is something each person works on internally before building it with anyone else. Within a year, the network had grown to more than 2,000 members between the ages of 14 and 30, spread across more than 100 countries and connected by that shared aim instead of any political position.

Dot Maver, a World Business Academy Fellow who nominated Miki for this series, has watched the approach up close. “Miki has dedicated herself to realizing Peace in herself, and inspiring others to do the same, and then to put Peace in Action in communities around the world,” Maver wrote. “It matters to me as a Peacebuilder who recognizes that peace begins with each one of us.”

The Global Youth Peace Journey

1,592 applicants and a three percent acceptance rate

In 2026, Miki launched the Peace Journey, a youth peace education program that invites participants to find their own path to peace through their passions, dreams, and fields of interest. It drew 1,592 applications from 104 countries, and only about three percent of applicants were accepted, according to Miki’s DailyGood essay. Maver served as a guide for the cohort.

The same year, Miki hosted a Ripples of Peace Retreat in London, presented at the Goi Peace Foundation Forum, and spoke at a Community of Living Ethics Conference in Italy. Maver, who was there, wrote that Miki “touched hearts and minds of all ages” and called her “a living demonstration of peace in action.”

Peace Journey 2027 applications open in December

The next Peace Journey begins in January 2027, with applications expected to open in early December. What Miki values most about the program is the permission it gives young people to start now. Participants learn, she said, that “they do not need to wait until they have extraordinary resources, influence, or experience to make a difference.” Peace, in her framing, can begin with who you are, how you treat others and what you choose to do today.

Youth peacebuilding from Rome to Japan

PeaceCream’s international debut

The Rome pop-up will be PeaceCream’s first appearance in front of an international audience, at a summit whose 2026 theme centers on artificial intelligence and peace. Miki hopes the experience sparks conversations between strangers and connects people across their differences, using one of the most universally loved foods as an entry point. “Our vision is to make peace not just something we talk about, but something we experience and want to share with others,” she said.

Four ambassadors return to the Goi Peace Foundation

Closer to home, four Youth Peace Ambassadors will travel to Japan for the Goi Peace Foundation’s annual forum and summit to share the projects they developed during the Peace Journey and compare notes on turning their ideas into action. Miki sees the gathering as a chance to link the ambassadors’ separate initiatives and show more young people that they can lead change themselves.

Miki began her undergraduate studies at Minerva University this fall and has brought the network with her, which means Youth Peace Ambassadors now grows alongside a student still working out her own questions about peace in public, much as her essay did. Her aim is to make peace something anyone can take part in, regardless of age, background, or circumstance, and the upcoming Peace Journey is the most direct way to do that. Young readers who want to apply can find the application, once it opens in December, on the Youth Peace Ambassadors website.

articles.title: Press release - Health and safety at work: 8 August to become European day of remembrance for victims of accidents at work
articles.summary: EU institutions sign a joint declaration establishing a European day of remembrance for victims of accidents at work.Committee on Employment and Social Affairs Source : © European Union, 2026 - EP
articles.content:
The European Parliament, Council and the Commission signed today a joint declaration establishing a European day of remembrance for victims of accidents at work. From 2027, this day will be observed each year on 8 August. The date marks the anniversary of the 1956 Bois du Cazier mining tragedy in Marcinelle, Belgium, in which 262 miners from across Europe lost their lives.

The establishment of this European day aims to:

honour the memory of victims of work accidents and occupational diseases

of work accidents and occupational diseases raise awareness among citizens, workers, businesses and institutions of the importance of prevention for occupational safety and health, and decent working conditions.

among citizens, workers, businesses and institutions of the importance of prevention for occupational safety and health, and decent working conditions. strengthen the commitment of the EU and its member states to eliminate work-related deaths, accidents and occupational diseases.

In their joint declaration, the three institutions committed to working together to promote safe and healthy working conditions and increase awareness among stakeholders and the general public of the importance of health and safety at work.

The initiative is also intended to complement the World Day for Safety and Health at Work, promoted by the International Labour Organization and celebrated on 28 April, from a specifically European perspective. While international observance draws global attention to safety and health in the workplace, a European day will increase awareness of workers' rights within the context of European integration and promote initiatives addressing the specific challenges in the European labour market.

Quotes

“Behind every workplace accident, there is a human life, a family and a community affected. The tragedy of Bois du Cazier reminds us, nearly seven decades later, of the devastating consequences of failing to protect workers. Remembering those who lost their lives must also mean acting to prevent such tragedies from happening again. With this European day of remembrance, we reaffirm our commitment to safe and dignified working conditions for everyone. No worker should ever have to risk their life to earn a living.”

Li Andersson, Chair of the European Parliament’s Committee on employment and social affairs (EMPL)

“Safe and healthy working conditions are a prerequisite for a healthy and productive workforce. Nobody across the EU should suffer from job-related accidents and diseases. I am extremely proud that we have signed today - during the Irish presidency - a joint declaration to observe 8 August each year as a European day in remembrance of the victims of accidents at work.”

Charlie McConalogue, Minister of State at the Department of Culture, Communications and Sport of Ireland

“Earning a living must never cost a life. On 8 August, Europe will remember the victims of workplace accidents. And this remembrance must drive action. We honour those who never came home by protecting those who go to work today.”

Roxana Mînzatu, Executive Vice-President of the European Commission for social rights and skills, quality jobs and preparedness

Background

Work-related accidents and deaths have decreased by over 70% in the last 30 years, thanks to the implementation of the EU occupational safety and health legislation and the EU strategic framework on health and safety at work 2021-2027. This framework combines legislation, guidelines, training, information, labour inspections, social dialogue and the exchange of best practices

The Commission calls on member states to pursue the ‘vision zero’ approach, with the aim of eliminating work-related deaths across the EU. Despite the progress, there were more than 3,300 fatal accidents at work and nearly 2.8 million non-fatal accidents at work were recorded in the EU in 2024 (Eurostat). In addition, over 170,000 people die each year from occupational diseases (European agency for safety and health at work). In its resolution of 21 May 2026 on the need to reduce work‑related fatalities, the European Parliament called for the establishment of a European day of remembrance for victims of accidents at work and stressed the need of prevention at work, safe and decent work, training, awareness-raising on emerging risks, social dialogue and the effective enforcement of existing legislation. At the EPSCO Council on 29 June 2026, several member states also called for the establishment of such a day, to be marked every year on 8 August.
articles.reasoning: The article reports the establishment of a European day of remembrance for victims of workplace accidents, a meaningful policy initiative that honors victims, raises awareness about occupational safety, and strengthens commitment to preventing work-related deaths and diseases across the EU. This has broad societal impact, promotes workers' rights, and is supported by detailed context and statistics.

articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Workplace accidents and diseases have caused many deaths and injuries in Europe over the years. Although safety has improved, thousands still suffer serious harm at work. The European Union has laws and plans to make work safer, but more action is needed.

**What happened** – On 8 August 2026, the European Parliament, Council, and Commission agreed to make 8 August a European day of remembrance for victims of accidents at work. This day will start in 2027 and honors those who lost their lives, especially recalling the 1956 mining disaster in Belgium where 262 miners died.

**Impact** – This new day will help people remember those affected by work accidents and encourage stronger safety rules. It will also raise awareness about the importance of protecting workers and preventing accidents and diseases. By focusing on Europe’s specific challenges, it supports workers’ rights and safer jobs across all member countries.

**What's next step** – Each year on 8 August, events and activities will promote health and safety at work. EU institutions and member states will work together to improve conditions and reduce accidents. This day will complement the global safety day on 28 April by focusing on Europe’s unique needs and progress.

**One-sentence takeaway** – Starting in 2027, Europe will mark 8 August every year to honor victims of workplace accidents and strengthen efforts to make work safer for everyone.

articles.content:
Click to expand Image Women take part in a demonstration against the military coup in Mandalay, Myanmar, on July 10, 2021. © 2021 STR/AFP via Getty Images

Every year during the 16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence women’s rights defenders come together to remember women facing violence—including those we have lost—and to renew the struggle for gender equality.

This year we face growing gender inequality, as the rights of women and girls are rolled back and threatened by authoritarianism and conflict in many countries. Across all regions, governments and powerful anti-rights movements seek to dismantle hard-won rights for women and girls. Technology is adding new dimensions to abuse, from online harassment and surveillance to digitally enabled threats, violence, and sexualized deepfake images; women politicians are often targeted.

In the United States and Russia, authorities are dismantling reproductive rights. In Africa, lawmakers, with support from foreign conservative groups, are promoting a charter aiming to roll back women’s rights across the continent. In Argentina, funding for preventing GBV has been scrapped.

As armed conflict increases across the globe, more women and girls are living in proximity to fighting. During conflict, women and girls face heightened risks of sexual and gender-based violence, displacement, and economic insecurity, often with little access to protection or justice. In Sudan and Democratic Republic of Congo, sexual violence is a common feature of ongoing conflict with survivors facing significant barriers to obtaining protection, services, and justice. In Myanmar, women political prisoners are tortured. Reproductive rights are a casualty of Israel’s closures in the West Bank, its ongoing blockade of the Gaza Strip, and its continued attacks on Palestinian health facilities.

But activists refuse to accept erosion of women’s rights.

In March, the Commission on the Status of Women called for strengthening access to justice for all women and girls. In April, the European Parliament passed a resolution calling for consent to be the determining factor in rape legislation across the EU. In November, Hungary announced it would ratify the Istanbul Convention, strengthening women’s rights protections. Activists from Afghanistan are fighting to have gender apartheid recognized as an international crime.

Activists are also pushing back against technology-facilitated abuse, demanding that companies protect, rather than endanger, women and girls. In different countries young women are leading protest movements to challenge corruption and authoritarianism.

Rights defenders will not lose hope.
articles.reasoning: The article highlights ongoing activism and significant policy progress aimed at protecting and advancing women's rights globally, despite serious challenges. It focuses on meaningful efforts by governments and activists to strengthen legal protections against gender-based violence and technology-facilitated abuse, with broad societal impact and detailed context.
articles.personality_title: Global activists unite to protect women’s rights amid rising challenges
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Every year, the 16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence bring people together to remember women affected by violence and to renew efforts for gender equality. This year, women’s rights face new threats from governments, conflicts, and technology around the world.

**What happened** – Despite increased risks, activists and governments have made important progress. In 2023, the European Parliament pushed for stronger rape laws based on consent, Hungary promised to follow an international treaty protecting women, and the United Nations called for better justice access for women and girls. Young women are also leading protests against corruption and authoritarian rule in several countries.

**Impact** – These actions are important because they respond to new problems like online abuse and political violence against women. They also challenge efforts by some governments to reduce women’s rights, such as cutting funding or limiting reproductive choices. By improving laws and raising awareness, these efforts help protect women from violence and give survivors better chances for justice.

**What’s next step** – Activists will keep pushing governments to enforce these new rules and fight back against technology that harms women. They aim to get more countries to join agreements like the Istanbul Convention and to have gender-based discrimination recognized as a serious international crime.

**One-sentence takeaway** – Despite growing threats, global activists and some governments are making important legal and social advances to protect women’s rights and fight gender-based violence.
articles.personality_title_fr: Des activistes du monde entier unis pour protéger les droits des femmes face à des défis croissants
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – Chaque année, les 16 jours d’activisme contre les violences basées sur le genre rassemblent les gens pour se souvenir des femmes victimes de violences et renouveler les efforts pour l’égalité des sexes. Cette année, les droits des femmes sont menacés par des gouvernements, des conflits et la technologie dans le monde entier.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – Malgré des risques accrus, les activistes et certains gouvernements ont fait des progrès importants. En 2023, le Parlement européen a renforcé les lois sur le viol basées sur le consentement, la Hongrie a promis de respecter une convention internationale protégeant les femmes, et l’ONU a appelé à un meilleur accès à la justice pour les femmes et les filles. De jeunes femmes mènent aussi des protestations contre la corruption et l’autoritarisme dans plusieurs pays.

**Impact** – Ces actions sont importantes car elles répondent à de nouveaux problèmes comme les abus en ligne et la violence politique contre les femmes. Elles contestent aussi les efforts de certains gouvernements pour réduire les droits des femmes, comme couper les budgets ou limiter les choix en matière de santé reproductive. En améliorant les lois et la sensibilisation, ces efforts aident à protéger les femmes et à offrir plus de justice aux survivantes.

**Prochaine étape** – Les activistes continueront de pousser les gouvernements à appliquer ces nouvelles règles et à lutter contre la technologie qui nuit aux femmes. Ils veulent que plus de pays rejoignent des accords comme la Convention d’Istanbul et que la discrimination basée sur le genre soit reconnue comme un crime international grave.

**Résumé en une phrase** – Malgré des menaces croissantes, des activistes et gouvernements du monde entier font des avancées importantes pour protéger les droits des femmes et lutter contre les violences basées sur le genre.
articles.personality_title_es: Activistas globales se unen para proteger los derechos de las mujeres frente a crecientes desafíos
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Cada año, los 16 Días de Activismo contra la Violencia de Género reúnen a personas para recordar a las mujeres afectadas por la violencia y renovar los esfuerzos por la igualdad de género. Este año, los derechos de las mujeres enfrentan nuevas amenazas de gobiernos, conflictos y tecnología en todo el mundo.

**Qué pasó** – A pesar de mayores riesgos, activistas y gobiernos lograron avances importantes. En 2023, el Parlamento Europeo impulsó leyes más fuertes sobre violación basadas en el consentimiento, Hungría prometió cumplir un tratado internacional que protege a las mujeres, y la ONU pidió mejor acceso a la justicia para mujeres y niñas. Jóvenes mujeres también lideran protestas contra la corrupción y el autoritarismo en varios países.

**Impacto** – Estas acciones son importantes porque responden a problemas nuevos como el abuso en línea y la violencia política contra las mujeres. También desafían los esfuerzos de algunos gobiernos por reducir los derechos de las mujeres, como recortar fondos o limitar las opciones reproductivas. Mejorar las leyes y crear conciencia ayuda a proteger a las mujeres y a ofrecer más justicia a las sobrevivientes.

**Próximo paso** – Los activistas seguirán presionando a los gobiernos para que apliquen estas nuevas reglas y combatan la tecnología que perjudica a las mujeres. Buscan que más países se unan a acuerdos como el Convenio de Estambul y que la discriminación de género se reconozca como un crimen internacional grave.

**Resumen en una frase** – A pesar de las crecientes amenazas, activistas y gobiernos en todo el mundo están logrando avances importantes para proteger los derechos de las mujeres y combatir la violencia de género.

articles.title: Press release - MEPs demand EU strategy to safeguard international justice system
articles.summary: On Wednesday, Parliament urged the EU to support the international justice system and protect institutions and defenders against foreign pressure.Committee on Foreign Affairs Source : © European Union, 2026 - EP
articles.content:
In a plenary report, MEPs highlighted the unprecedented threats faced by the international justice system and in particular the International Criminal Court (ICC), as they are subject to coercive pressure, unilateral sanctions and campaigns to undermine their credibility and independence. Since last year, the US Administration has imposed sanctions on ICC officials, freezing their assets and prohibiting any material or financial support. Other measures target UN mandate holders and partner non-governmental organisations, they add.



Strengthen the international justice system and protect EU sovereignty



The report calls for the update and activation of the "blocking statute" to protect European operators against the extraterritorial effects of third-party coercive measures. MEPs note that the US sanctions have created a climate of concern among European banks, insurance companies and digital service providers leading to "overcompliance" that impedes essential payments and services relating to international justice.



They therefore propose reducing the EU’s structural dependencies on non-European financial and digital infrastructure and using the anti-coercion instrument. Parliament insists on the importance of working with partner democracies to mitigate these pressures, through trade agreements and political dialogue. It also stresses the need to facilitate visas for witnesses and human rights defenders working on accountability in order to preserve the integrity of legal evidence before international courts.



Reaffirming the universality of the ICC, it calls on the European Council to explicitly integrate the Rome Statute into the EU acquis, while emphasising the vital role international justice plays in upholding the rule of law, ensuring accountability, and protecting victims everywhere.

Call for a coordinated EU response



MEPs insist that international justice is a pillar of the EU’s strategic autonomy and call for a coordinated response to ensure that impunity is not tolerated for the most serious crimes.



Plenary asks the Commission and the EU’s High Representative for Foreign Affairs to propose a strategy and an action plan, including, in particular, an evaluation of existing tools to fill gaps, concrete protection mechanisms for judges, prosecutors, witnesses and victims, predictable and robust financial support for international justice mechanisms, and better coordination between EU member states, Eurojust, and UN investigative mechanisms. The Commission should present an annual report on the implementation of the strategy, the impact of foreign sanctions and the use of EU funds allocated to international justice, MEPs add.

Quote



Rapporteur Mounir Satouri (Greens/EFA, FR) declared : " This report is Parliament’s answer to the current attacks on international law and the US Administration’s sanctions against the ICC. We stand for EU sovereignty and international justice without double standards. Now it’s up to the executive to act firmly: trigger the Blocking Statute as a matter of urgency and launch a coordinated strategy to protect the ICC."

The report was adopted by 438 votes for, 168 against and 38 abstentions.



Parliament awarded the 2026 Sakharov Prize for Freedom of Thought to the ICC and its officials on 22 October. The award ceremony will take place on Tuesday 15 December, during Parliament’s plenary session in Strasbourg.

This action promotes the rule of law, accountability for serious crimes, and protection of human rights defenders and victims on a broad scale. The detailed proposals and political commitment indicate a meaningful and substantive response with significant positive impact for global justice and human rights.
articles.personality_title: EU Parliament pushes to protect international justice from foreign pressure
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – The International Criminal Court (ICC) and other international justice bodies are facing growing pressure from foreign governments, including sanctions by the United States that freeze assets and restrict support for ICC officials. These actions threaten the independence and work of these institutions.

**What happened** – On Wednesday, the European Parliament voted to demand a strong EU strategy to defend the international justice system. They called for updating laws like the "blocking statute" to shield European companies from foreign sanctions and urged reducing EU reliance on non-European financial and digital systems. The Parliament also asked the European Commission and EU foreign affairs leaders to create a detailed plan to protect judges, witnesses, and human rights defenders involved in international justice.

**Impact** – This is a clear step by the EU to defend the rule of law and ensure accountability for serious crimes worldwide. By pushing for legal protections and financial support, the EU aims to keep international courts independent and effective. It also supports human rights defenders and victims by making it easier for them to participate in justice processes.

**What's next step** – The European Commission will develop a strategy and action plan based on Parliament’s demands, including yearly reports on progress. The EU will work with other democracies to strengthen international justice and protect it from coercion. A ceremony awarding the ICC the 2026 Sakharov Prize will highlight this commitment.

**One-sentence takeaway** – The European Parliament is leading efforts to safeguard international justice by demanding stronger EU laws and coordinated action against foreign pressures on courts like the ICC.
articles.personality_title_fr: Le Parlement européen agit pour protéger la justice internationale des pressions étrangères
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – La Cour pénale internationale (CPI) et d'autres institutions de justice internationale subissent des pressions croissantes, notamment des sanctions des États-Unis qui gelant les avoirs et limitent le soutien aux responsables de la CPI. Ces mesures menacent leur indépendance.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – Mercredi, le Parlement européen a voté pour exiger une stratégie forte de l’UE afin de défendre le système de justice international. Il a demandé la mise à jour de la « loi de blocage » pour protéger les entreprises européennes des sanctions étrangères et la réduction de la dépendance de l’UE aux infrastructures financières et numériques hors d’Europe. Le Parlement a aussi appelé la Commission européenne et les responsables des affaires étrangères à élaborer un plan d’action pour protéger juges, témoins et défenseurs des droits humains.

**Impact** – Il s’agit d’une étape claire de l’UE pour défendre l’état de droit et garantir la responsabilité pour les crimes graves dans le monde. En renforçant les protections juridiques et le soutien financier, l’UE veut préserver l’indépendance et l’efficacité des tribunaux internationaux. Elle facilite aussi la participation des victimes et défenseurs des droits humains.

**Prochaine étape** – La Commission européenne préparera une stratégie et un plan d’action basés sur les demandes du Parlement, avec des rapports annuels. L’UE travaillera avec d’autres démocraties pour renforcer la justice internationale et la protéger des pressions. Une cérémonie de remise du prix Sakharov 2026 à la CPI soulignera cet engagement.

**Une phrase clé** – Le Parlement européen mène les efforts pour protéger la justice internationale en demandant des lois plus fortes et une action coordonnée contre les pressions étrangères sur la CPI.
articles.personality_title_es: El Parlamento Europeo impulsa la protección de la justicia internacional frente a presiones extranjeras
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – La Corte Penal Internacional (CPI) y otros organismos de justicia internacional enfrentan crecientes presiones de gobiernos extranjeros, incluidas sanciones de Estados Unidos que congelan activos y limitan el apoyo a funcionarios de la CPI. Estas acciones amenazan la independencia de estas instituciones.

**Qué pasó** – El miércoles, el Parlamento Europeo votó para exigir una estrategia fuerte de la UE para defender el sistema de justicia internacional. Pidieron actualizar leyes como el "estatuto de bloqueo" para proteger a empresas europeas de sanciones extranjeras y reducir la dependencia de la UE en sistemas financieros y digitales no europeos. También solicitaron a la Comisión Europea y a los líderes de asuntos exteriores que creen un plan para proteger a jueces, testigos y defensores de derechos humanos.

**Impacto** – Esto representa un paso claro de la UE para defender el estado de derecho y asegurar la rendición de cuentas por crímenes graves en todo el mundo. Al promover protecciones legales y apoyo financiero, la UE busca mantener la independencia y eficacia de los tribunales internacionales. También facilita la participación de víctimas y defensores.

**Próximo paso** – La Comisión Europea desarrollará una estrategia y plan de acción basados en las demandas del Parlamento, con informes anuales sobre el progreso. La UE trabajará con otras democracias para fortalecer la justicia internacional y protegerla de presiones. Una ceremonia para entregar el Premio Sájarov 2026 a la CPI destacará este compromiso.

**Una frase clave** – El Parlamento Europeo lidera los esfuerzos para proteger la justicia internacional exigiendo leyes más fuertes y acción coordinada contra las presiones extranjeras sobre la CPI.
